lesson.menu_desc: Time clauses for instructions (once you've / as soon as / until + present perfect), app and process words, walking someone through it -- 30 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 37 — Step by Step
lesson.title_tag: Professor View — Vanessa Giuriati | Lesson 37 — Step by Step
lesson.grammar_point: time clauses with the present perfect for instructions (once you've / as soon as you've / until you've + imperative)

listenings.text: Have you ever followed instructions that seemed clear to the writer, but not to you? Good instructions have three secrets. First, one step means one action. Don't say, open the app, log in and find the report. Say, open the app. Then, once you've opened it, log in. Second, tell people what they will see, so they know they are on the right track. For example, once you've tapped Save, you'll see a green message. Third, give the warning before the step, not after it. Say, make sure you save the file before you close it. Don't say, oh, you should have saved it. And at the end, don't ask, is that clear? Most people say yes, even when it isn't. Ask, what will you do first? Their answer tells you everything.

Welcome back to the kitchen. Today, Brazilian cheese bread, the easy way. First, heat the oven to three hundred and fifty degrees. Put the milk, the oil and a little salt in a pan, and wait until it has started to boil. As soon as it has boiled, pour it over the tapioca flour and mix well. Now, be careful. Don't add the eggs until the mixture has cooled down a little, or they will cook. Once you've added the eggs, add the cheese, lots of cheese. Then wet your hands and make small balls. After you've put them on the tray, bake them for about twenty-five minutes, until they're golden. The first time, it's a little messy. But by the third time, you'll get the hang of it.

extra_audio.text: First, I ask what the person already knows. Then I give one step at a time: once you've done that, do this. After that, I say what they will see on the screen. Next, I give the warning before the step: make sure you save it. In the end, I ask: what will you do first?
